title: Task Horizon Curve Explorer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AI-Native Schools
description: Calculate a model's chance of finishing tasks of different lengths from its 50 percent time horizon, then move the horizon and watch the success curve shift.

educational.topic: Success curves and the 50 percent time horizon
learningObjectives: The learner will calculate a model's chance of completing tasks of different human working times from its 50 percent time horizon, to within 2 percentage points, and identify the task length at which the chance reaches 80 percent.
prerequisites: Human working time, task success rate, task horizon, 50 percent time horizon, and the rule P = 1/(1 + t/H), from the section "METR and the Task-Horizon Idea" in Chapter 4.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Commit three calculations before the slider unlocks, then explore the whole curve
keyQuestions: What is the chance of success at t = H?
At what task length does the chance reach 80 percent?
commonMisconceptions: A model with a 1-hour horizon is reliable on all tasks up to 1 hour
Success drops to zero just past the horizon
The 80 percent horizon is about the same as the 50 percent horizon
assessmentOpportunities: H = 60 minutes. What is the chance on a 15-minute task?
Where is the 80 percent point for any H?
Does the chance drop to zero just past the horizon?
Is a model with a 1-hour horizon reliable on all tasks up to an hour?

controls.name: Your answer box and Check
controls.description: type a percent or a number of minutes and press Check (or Enter). Two attempts per question; only the first counts.

controls.name: Next
controls.description: moves on; after question 3 it unlocks the slider.

controls.name: Horizon H
controls.description: slider from 15 to 960 minutes in steps of 15.

controls.name: Redo challenges and Defaults
controls.description: start the questions again, or return H to 60 minutes.
